  - Figure 1(b),(c): 5^{\circ} rotation on pitch / roll axis -> minor change in 2D image

- SGAT4PASS
  - SGA framework + SGA validation

  - SGA image projection: images with 3D disturbance -> 3D robustness
  - SDPE: deformable operation for distortions + SGA intra- and inter-offset constraints
  - panorama-aware loss: pixel density difference
  - SGA validation: different 3D disturbances, average performance + variance
  - Stanford2D3D: about 2% (traditional metrics) and 6% (SGA metrics) improvements

steps.name: partial_draft
steps.text:
In recent years more and more practical applications are based on 360^{\circ} cameras, for example holistic sensing in autonomous vehicles and immersive viewing in augmented reality and virtual reality devices. Panoramic images have an ultra-wide angle of view and give complete scene perception in many real-world scenarios, so they are getting more attention in the computer vision research community. Panoramic semantic segmentation (PASS) is essential for omnidirectional scene understanding, because it gives pixel-wise analysis for panoramic images and it offers a dense prediction technical route to get 360^{\circ} perception of the surrounding scenes.

Most of the existing PASS approaches use equirectangular projection (ERP) to convert the original 360^{\circ} data into 2D panoramic images. But these methods often have two main problems: large image distortions, and a lack of Spherical Geometry-Aware (SGA) robustness against 3D disturbance. Because of these problems neural networks only learn suboptimal solutions for panoramic segmentation. Some recent works take the serious distortions into account in their models and are the current state-of-the-art (SOTA), but they still don't pay enough attention to the SGA properties of the original 360^{\circ} data, so their performance degrades even with small projection disturbance. Figure 1(b) and Figure 1(c) show that applying 5^{\circ} rotation on the pitch or roll axis of the original 360^{\circ} data only gives minor changes in the 2D panoramic images. But in Figure 1(e), Figure 1(f), and Figure 1(d), the performance of Trans4PASS+ (the blue lines) drops a lot (about 4%) and the variance increases by almost 2 orders of magnitude. This is because the axis rotations lead to different spherical geometry relations between the pixels in the projected panoramic images, and the existing methods fail to adapt to this. Besides disturbance, ERP also adds boundaries to panoramic images that the original 360^{\circ} data does not have. Some adjacent pixels get disconnected and some objects get separated, which is a severe issue, especially for semantic segmentation. There is also a difference in pixel sampling density between the original 360^{\circ} data and the projection image, e.g., pixels are over sampled in the antarctic and arctic areas of the 2D panoramic images. All of these issues make panoramic semantic segmentation a challenging task, and these characteristics should be studied well in order to design a robust model that adapts to disturbance, disconnection, uneven density and other SGA properties.

- SGAT4PASS = SGA framework + SGA validation
  - framework: SGA image projection (training), Spherical Deformable Patch Embedding (SDPE), panorama-aware loss
  - SGA image projection: images with 3D disturbance -> 3D robustness
  - SDPE: deformable operation for distortions + SGA intra- and inter-offset constraints
  - panorama-aware loss: pixel density difference between 360^{\circ} data and 2D images
  - SGA validation: different 3D disturbances, average performance + variance
  - Stanford2D3D: about 2% (traditional metrics) and 6% (SGA metrics) improvements

Contributions:
- SGAT4PASS, robustness model; SGA image projection for 3D disturbance from ERP
- SDPE for distortion; panorama-aware loss for oversampling
- experiments on popular benchmark, traditional + SGA metrics, effectiveness of each part

steps.name: rough_draft
steps.text:
In recent years more and more practical applications are based on 360^{\circ} cameras, for example holistic sensing in autonomous vehicles and immersive viewing in augmented reality and virtual reality devices. Panoramic images have an ultra-wide angle of view and give complete scene perception in many real-world scenarios, so they are getting more attention in the computer vision research community. Panoramic semantic segmentation (PASS) is essential for omnidirectional scene understanding, because it gives pixel-wise analysis for panoramic images and it offers a dense prediction technical route to get 360^{\circ} perception of the surrounding scenes.

Most of the existing PASS approaches use equirectangular projection (ERP) to convert the original 360^{\circ} data into 2D panoramic images. But these methods often have two main problems: large image distortions, and a lack of Spherical Geometry-Aware (SGA) robustness against 3D disturbance. Because of these problems neural networks only learn suboptimal solutions for panoramic segmentation. Some recent works take the serious distortions into account in their models and are the current state-of-the-art (SOTA), but they still don't pay enough attention to the SGA properties of the original 360^{\circ} data, so their performance degrades even with small projection disturbance. Figure 1(b) and Figure 1(c) show that applying 5^{\circ} rotation on the pitch or roll axis of the original 360^{\circ} data only gives minor changes in the 2D panoramic images. But in Figure 1(e), Figure 1(f), and Figure 1(d), the performance of Trans4PASS+ (the blue lines) drops a lot (about 4%) and the variance increases by almost 2 orders of magnitude. This is because the axis rotations lead to different spherical geometry relations between the pixels in the projected panoramic images, and the existing methods fail to adapt to this. Besides disturbance, ERP also adds boundaries to panoramic images that the original 360^{\circ} data does not have. Some adjacent pixels get disconnected and some objects get separated, which is a severe issue, especially for semantic segmentation. There is also a difference in pixel sampling density between the original 360^{\circ} data and the projection image, e.g., pixels are over sampled in the antarctic and arctic areas of the 2D panoramic images. All of these issues make panoramic semantic segmentation a challenging task, and these characteristics should be studied well in order to design a robust model that adapts to disturbance, disconnection, uneven density and other SGA properties.

To improve robustness and take SGA properties into account, we propose a new model, Spherical Geometry-Aware Transformer for PAnoramic Semantic Segmentation (SGAT4PASS), which has the SGA framework and SGA validation. The SGA framework has SGA image projection in the training process, Spherical Deformable Patch Embedding (SDPE), and a panorama-aware loss. SGA image projection gives images with 3D disturbance to make the model more robust in 3D. SDPE improves the patch embedding so that it considers not only the image distortions with a deformable operation but also spherical geometry with SGA intra- and inter-offset constraints. The panorama-aware loss handles the difference in pixel density between the original 360^{\circ} data and the 2D panoramic images. We also propose a new validation method, SGA validation, to evaluate the 3D robustness of different models comprehensively. It considers different 3D disturbances for the input images and measures the average performance and the variance for comparison. Extensive experiments on the popular Stanford2D3D panoramic datasets show that our approach gets about 2% and 6% improvements on traditional metrics and SGA metrics, respectively.

Our contributions are the following:

- • We propose SGAT4PASS, a robustness model for the PASS task, which uses SGA image projection to deal with the 3D disturbance problem caused by ERP.

- • We introduce SDPE, which combines spherical geometry with deformable operation to deal better with panoramic image distortion. We also propose panorama-aware loss to ease the oversampling problem.

- • We evaluate SGAT4PASS on the popular benchmark and do extensive experiments with both traditional metrics and the proposed SGA metrics, which show that each part of the framework is effective.

steps.name: revised_draft
steps.text:
There has been a growing trend of practical applications based on 360^{\circ} cameras in recent years, including holistic sensing in autonomous vehicles [1,2,3,4,5,6,7] and immersive viewing in augmented reality and virtual reality devices [8,9,10]. Panoramic images with an ultra-wide angle of view deliver complete scene perception in many real-world scenarios, and have thus drawn increasing attention in the computer vision research community. Panoramic semantic segmentation (PASS) is essential for omnidirectional scene understanding, as it gives pixel-wise analysis for panoramic images and offers a dense prediction technical route to acquiring 360^{\circ} perception of surrounding scenes [11].

Most existing PASS approaches use equirectangular projection (ERP) [12,13] to convert original 360^{\circ} data to 2D panoramic images. However, these methods often suffer from two main problems: large image distortions and a lack of Spherical Geometry-Aware (SGA) robustness that resists 3D disturbance. These problems lead neural networks to learn only suboptimal solutions for panoramic segmentation [14,15]. Although some recent works [16,17] take serious distortions into account in their models and are the current state-of-the-art (SOTA), they still pay too little attention to the SGA properties of the original 360^{\circ} data, resulting in performance degradation even with small projection disturbance. As shown in Figure 1(b) and Figure 1(c), applying 5^{\circ} rotation on the pitch or roll axis of original 360^{\circ} data causes only minor changes in 2D panoramic images. However, as shown in Figure 1(e), Figure 1(f), and Figure 1(d), the performance of Trans4PASS+ [17] (the blue lines) drops a lot (about 4%), and the variance increases by almost 2 orders of magnitude, because the axis rotations lead to different spherical geometry relations between pixels in the projected panoramic images, which existing methods fail to adapt to. Besides disturbance, ERP also introduces boundaries to panoramic images that the original 360^{\circ} data do not have. Some adjacent pixels are disconnected and some objects are separated, which is a severe issue, especially for semantic segmentation. Furthermore, the pixel sampling density differs between the original 360^{\circ} data and its projection image, e.g., pixels are over sampled in the antarctic and arctic areas of 2D panoramic images. All these issues make panoramic semantic segmentation a challenging task, and these characteristics should be well studied to design a robust model that adapts to disturbance, disconnection, uneven density, and other SGA properties.

To improve robustness and take SGA properties into account, we propose a novel model, i.e., Spherical Geometry-Aware Transformer for PAnoramic Semantic Segmentation (SGAT4PASS), equipped with the SGA framework and SGA validation. The proposed SGA framework includes SGA image projection in the training process, Spherical Deformable Patch Embedding (SDPE), and a panorama-aware loss. SGA image projection provides images with 3D disturbance to improve the 3D robustness of the model. SDPE improves the patch embedding so that it considers not only the image distortions with deformable operation but also spherical geometry with SGA intra- and inter-offset constraints. The panorama-aware loss deals with the difference in pixel density between the original 360^{\circ} data and its corresponding 2D panoramic images. Moreover, we propose a new validation method, i.e., SGA validation, to comprehensively evaluate the 3D robustness of various models; it considers different 3D disturbances for input images and measures the average performance and the variance for comparisons. Extensive experimental results on the popular Stanford2D3D panoramic datasets [18] demonstrate that our approach achieves about 2% and 6% improvements on traditional metrics and SGA metrics, respectively.

The contributions of this paper are summarized as follows:

- • We propose SGAT4PASS, a robustness model for the PASS task, which uses SGA image projection to deal with the 3D disturbance issue caused by ERP.

- • We introduce SDPE to combine spherical geometry with deformable operation to better handle panoramic image distortion. We also propose a panorama-aware loss to ease the oversampling problem.

- • We evaluate SGAT4PASS on the popular benchmark and perform extensive experiments with both traditional metrics and the proposed SGA metrics, which demonstrate the effectiveness of each part of the framework.
